input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# Platform Operator midstream repository onboarding

## Description

Establish the midstream repository for the Platform Operator under opendatahub-io so that FIPS crypto
remediation work on the operator has a place to land. The Platform Operator has no architecture-context
file and is therefore treated as not yet in the platform inventory; this epic provisions the repository
foundation that the build pipeline onboarding and the implementation work build on.

## Scope

- Fork/create the Platform Operator midstream repository under the opendatahub-io organization, following
  the established midstream fork pattern used by other platform components (e.g. opendatahub-io/kserve).
- Set up the initial branch structure and basic repository configuration (owners, branch protection,
  contribution workflow) consistent with other opendatahub-io midstream repositories.
- Verify the repository builds from source at the forked revision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Platform Operator midstream repository exists under opendatahub-io and is accessible to the owning
  team.
- The repository builds from source at its initial revision (basic build, not yet the Konflux pipeline).
- Repository configuration (branch structure, ownership) matches the opendatahub-io midstream conventions.

## HLR Traceability

- No direct HLR. Enabling epic: it provides the repository that the Platform Operator FIPS crypto
  remediation (HLR-1) requires; it inherits P0 from the P0 remediation work it enables.

# Platform Operator transitive dependency license validation

## Description

Run license validation over the Platform Operator's transitive dependencies so that the FIPS remediation
proceeds against a dependency set that is known to be distributable. This runs in parallel with the
repository onboarding — it has independent inputs — and gates the general remediation work: a license
failure changes the dependency set and therefore the remediation approach.

## Scope

- Configure and run license scanning over the Platform Operator's transitive dependency tree.
- Produce a license report covering all dependencies of the operator images in scope for FIPS remediation.
- Document any problematic licenses and their resolution (replacement dependency, exception request, or
  removal) before the remediation work consumes the dependency set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A complete license scan of the Platform Operator transitive dependencies exists, covering every
  dependency of the images in scope for the FIPS work.
- Every license flagged as incompatible with product distribution has a documented resolution.
- The license report is available to the remediation work as an input.

## HLR Traceability

- No direct HLR. Enabling epic for the Platform Operator FIPS crypto remediation (HLR-1); P0 by priority
  inheritance from the remediation it gates.

# Platform Operator Konflux build pipeline onboarding

## Description

Onboard the Platform Operator midstream repository to Konflux so its images are built by the platform
build pipeline, producing the signed images and build attestations that the FIPS compliance evidence
package consumes. This starts after the repository exists and runs in parallel with the FIPS crypto
remediation — the pipeline configuration does not depend on the remediated code, and the remediation does
not wait for the pipeline.

## Scope

- Onboard the Platform Operator repository to Konflux using the standard onboarding recipe.
- Configure the build pipeline to produce the Platform Operator container images with the standard
  attestation generation (provenance, SBOM).
- Get the pipeline green on the main branch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Platform Operator repository is onboarded to Konflux.
- The Konflux pipeline builds the Platform Operator images and completes green on the main branch.
- Builds produce signed attestations (provenance and SBOM) consumable by the compliance evidence work.

## HLR Traceability

- No direct HLR. Enabling epic: the build attestations it produces are required content for the FIPS
  compliance evidence package (HLR-2), and the pipeline carries the FIPS regression gating check (HLR-3)
  for Platform Operator builds. P0 by inheritance from the P0 evidence work it feeds.

# Platform Operator FIPS crypto remediation

## Description

Remediate the Platform Operator images so they run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using
validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in the request path. This is the Platform
Operator half of the serving-stack FIPS remediation. It starts once the midstream repository exists and
license validation has cleared the dependency set; it runs in parallel with the Konflux pipeline
onboarding — their coupling is enforced by the build-pipeline acceptance criterion below, not by a
scheduling dependency.

## Scope

- Audit the Platform Operator images and their dependency tree to identify every linked cryptographic
  library and classify each as validated or non-validated.
- Replace or rebuild against validated crypto modules for every non-validated usage in the request path.
- Verify the remediated images function correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- Publish the remediated images through the Platform Operator build pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A crypto module inventory for every Platform Operator image in scope exists, classifying each linked
  cryptographic library as validated or non-validated.
- No non-validated cryptographic library remains linked in the request path of any remediated Platform
  Operator image.
- Functional tests pass with the remediated images running on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster.
- The build pipeline is green for the remediated images (first execution of the remediated code through
  the Platform Operator Konflux pipeline succeeds).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto
  modules — Platform Operator portion.

# KServe serving-stack image FIPS crypto remediation

## Description

Remediate the KServe serving-stack images so they run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using
validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in the request path. KServe already has
midstream repositories (opendatahub-io/kserve) and is Konflux-onboarded, so this work starts immediately
with no onboarding prerequisites.

## Scope

- Audit the KServe component images and the serving data plane images for every linked cryptographic
  library, classifying each as validated or non-validated.
- Replace or rebuild against validated crypto modules for every non-validated usage in the request path.
- Verify the remediated images function correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters in both serving
  deployment modes (serverless and raw deployment).
- Publish the remediated images through the existing KServe build pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A crypto module inventory for every KServe and serving data plane image in scope exists, classifying
  each linked cryptographic library as validated or non-validated.
- No non-validated cryptographic library remains linked in the request path of any remediated image.
- Functional tests pass with the remediated images running on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, in both
  serverless and raw deployment modes.
- The existing KServe Konflux build pipeline is green for the remediated images.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto
  modules — KServe and serving data plane portion.

# FIPS regression gating CI check for serving-stack builds

## Description

Add a gating CI check that fails any serving-stack build which reintroduces non-validated cryptographic
usage, so the FIPS remediation cannot silently regress. This is pipeline/CI configuration work,
independent of the image remediation itself — it configures the build pipelines the serving-stack images
are built through, including the KServe pipelines and the Platform Operator pipeline once it exists.

## Scope

- Define the detection criterion for non-validated crypto usage in built images (linked cryptographic
  modules not on the validated-modules list established by the remediation work).
- Implement the check and wire it as a gating (required) step in the serving-stack build pipelines,
  covering both the KServe serving-stack builds and the Platform Operator builds.
- Include a negative test proving the check fails a build that reintroduces a non-validated crypto usage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gating check exists in the serving-stack build pipelines that fails any build whose images link
  non-validated cryptographic modules in the request path.
- The check is gating (blocks merge/ship), not advisory.
- Verified by negative test: intentionally reintroducing a non-validated crypto usage into a serving-stack
  build causes the check to fail that build.
- The check runs on both KServe and Platform Operator serving-stack builds.
- The detection criterion is defined against the validated-modules list established by the serving-stack
  image remediation work (the crypto module inventories classifying each linked cryptographic library as
  validated or non-validated): a build fails if and only if its images link a cryptographic module in the
  request path that is not on that list. The list is consumed as a configuration reference, and the
  negative test above is run against a module known to be off the list.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): CI enforces FIPS regressions — a gating check fails any serving-stack build that
  reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

# FIPS compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

Assemble the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving stack — module inventory, build
attestations, and test results — and submit it through the security review board process to the external
accredited certification lab. The engineering completion point is a complete, internally validated
evidence package that is submitted and accepted for triage; the lab's certification decision and the
review board's cadence are externally controlled and are tracked as schedule risks, not deliverables.

## Scope

- Consolidate the module inventory from the serving-stack crypto audits (KServe, serving data plane, and
  Platform Operator images) into a single compliance inventory of cryptographic modules.
- Collect the build attestations (provenance, SBOM) produced by the serving-stack build pipelines for the
  remediated images, including the Platform Operator pipeline attestations.
- Collect the FIPS-mode test results demonstrating correct operation of the remediated images on
  FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- Assemble the evidence package in the format required by the security review board and the certification
  lab, and drive it through the security review board milestone sign-offs to submission to the lab.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the complete module inventory, the build attestations for every
  remediated serving-stack image, and the FIPS-mode test results.
- The evidence package is internally validated for completeness and consistency against the submission
  requirements before hand-off.
- The evidence package is submitted through the security review board process to the external certification
  lab and accepted for triage.

### Risks / Notes

- The accredited lab's historical turnaround is six to nine months, and the security review board meets on
  a fixed cadence; both are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. They
  dominate the schedule of the certification outcome but do not gate any engineering deliverable in this
  decomposition.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is
  assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab.

# FIPS support posture documentation

## Description

Author user-facing documentation stating the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and the
cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters. This is substantive new
documentation content, so it is a separate docs-authoring work stream that runs after the implementation
work it describes.

## Scope

- New documentation topic(s) covering:
  - The FIPS 140-3 support posture of the model serving stack (what is supported, and what is not in
    scope — workbenches, pipelines, and training are covered by separate strategies).
  - Cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation (FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, validated crypto
    modules).
  - Any user-visible behavioral notes arising from the remediation (e.g. crypto module constraints in the
    request path).
- Follow the Red Hat docs content process for authoring, building, and publishing the topic(s).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack.
- Published documentation states the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented remediation (reviewed by the serving-stack
  engineering teams for accuracy against what was built).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites.
